entries.reason: a double setup has its targets in place before the first sample whatever the rate and the threshold are, so the two rate arguments of this call are stored and change nothing - measured, and a difference from the header's wording
entries.effect: each named coefficient takes its target at once, and interp_rate and interp_threshold are recorded with it and change no answer. Measured with a b0 going from 1 to 9: the rates and thresholds 0.1/0.25, 0.9/0.25, 0.5/100 and 0/0.25 all answer 9 from the first sample, where the single-precision setup answers 1, 8.2, 9 and 1, 1.8, 2.52 for the first two In a cascade the walk differs from a single section's: a coefficient lands on its target when what is left of the distance is at most interp_threshold *and* every section after it has landed too, so the snap travels backwards through the cascade. Measured over eleven host cases at rates of 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 and thresholds of 0.1 to 0.5, and the port answers every one of them
